gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-suse: Shantell Sans has a wide, friendly mouth and a nib that never changes width. SUSE sits beneath it in sans-serif curves with open bowls, so the loose heading gets a tidy, approachable partner.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-suse-mono: Shantell Sans leads with one fixed line width through every curve. SUSE Mono follows in sans-serif, each letter given extra room on both sides, so a long passage moves slowly and clearly, one glyph at a time.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-tajawal: Tajawal brings a broad, open hook to its c and a sans-serif calm. Shantell Sans hangs above it with a gentle monotone line and a wide mouth, loose and expressive against that tidy text.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-tasa-explorer: Expressive is the first word that fits Shantell Sans, whose round bowls keep their outline unswollen. And TASA Explorer, a plain sans with curve ends that stop like lifted brush strokes, lets those big, short headings do the talking.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-tasa-orbiter: TASA Orbiter keeps every small counter unclogged, a clean, professional sans-serif under Shantell Sans, whose signage-like plainness runs through every line weight. Clarity is what they share.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-teachers: Teachers feels like thin steel rod bent into letters, with ink strokes tapering out before they touch. And Shantell Sans, with its wide mouth and fixed nib, draws bolder, rounder shapes where that plain sans stays modern and light.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-telex: Telex is a sans-serif with curvy, unclamped letters that loosen up each line of text. And a longer passage in it should read smoothly beneath Shantell Sans, whose unshaded, constant strokes carry the headline.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-tenor-sans: Cable-like strokes meet soft pencil. Shantell Sans holds every stroke at one thickness for bold display work, while Tenor Sans lets light thick-thin shifts and c tips that never touch carry the text.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-tirra: A wide-mouthed display face drawn like neatly bent pipe cleaner, Shantell Sans keeps its nib fixed throughout. Tirra's round sans forms, like open parentheses, do the quieter work of text.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-titillium-web: Approachable is the mood Titillium Web sets, with stroke ends set far apart, though Shantell Sans, free of thin or swelling strokes, owns the headline. The plain sans handles text.
